title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
gist: At GOTO Copenhagen, Adam Tornhill argues AI coding velocity gains vanish within ~two months as complexity rises, and that healthy code makes LLM agents perform better and use 40-45% fewer tokens. Agentic refactoring fed by a code-health MCP can lift fix rates to 90-100%, making code health a cost and adoption lever for enterprise agentic coding.

insights.claim: A study of 1000+ open-source projects found AI-assisted velocity rose in the first few weeks but the gains were fully cancelled out after two months by a massive increase in code complexity.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Headline productivity claims for AI coding tools may overstate durable ROI; watch for vendors selling maintainability/safeguarding as the bottleneck.
insights.quote: AI operates in a self-harm mode, often writing code it cannot reliably maintain later.
insights.locator: Tornhill mentioned a study done on 1000+ open-source projects

insights.claim: Developers using agentic AI can complete tasks two to three times faster, and agents help them unblock themselves and reduce coordination needs, even though developing with agents is harder than writing code manually.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Short-run productivity gains are real, which sustains adoption demand even as long-run maintenance costs rise.
insights.locator: Developing software with agents is significantly harder

insights.claim: 95% of the costs of any software project come after the first release, so AI's speed at prototyping does not address where most software cost sits.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Value in AI dev tooling will migrate from code generation to maintenance, quality and architecture tooling.
insights.quote: Building a prototype was never the hard problem in software; 95% of the costs for any software project come after the first release.
insights.locator: Building a prototype was never the hard problem

themes.theme: Code health as AI performance and cost lever

insights.claim: Pre-AI research shows developers in healthy code can be up to 10x faster than in unhealthy code, with 15x lower defect risk and code reviews completing twice as fast.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Code-quality metrics have quantified economic impact that can justify tooling spend.
insights.locator: Code health measures how easy code is to understand

insights.claim: Large language models perform consistently better in healthy code, and healthy code lets AI do the same work with 40% to 45% fewer tokens, making code quality a direct lever on AI inference spend.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Enterprises facing rising token bills have a cost-optimization reason to invest in refactoring and code-health tooling.
insights.quote: Healthy code is also financially viable code, with healthy code, you can do things with 40% to 45% fewer tokens
insights.locator: Healthy code is also financially viable code

insights.claim: The average codebase scores 5.15 on code health while AI-friendly code starts at 9.5, so most enterprise codebases sit far below the threshold where agents work well.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Technical debt is a bottleneck on enterprise agentic-coding adoption, implying a large remediation market.
insights.locator: The average codebase has a code health of 5.15

insights.claim: Unaided, an agent like Claude can at best fix roughly 50% of code-health issues in low-health code, and only about 20% once code health improves, because the AI becomes conservative and makes small changes.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Raw frontier models are insufficient for refactoring; differentiated value lies in feedback tooling layered on top.
insights.quote: AI tends to become conservative, doing small changes that don’t really move the needle on code quality.
insights.locator: As a best-case scenario, an agent can fix roughly 50%

insights.claim: Supplying code-health data to an agent via an MCP server can raise refactoring fix rates to 90%-100%, turning agentic refactoring into a predictable, mechanical process at scale.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Objective-metric MCP servers are a high-leverage add-on category for coding agents; watch code-quality vendors integrating with agent ecosystems.
insights.locator: Adding an MCP with code health data

insights.claim: Scaling agentic refactoring requires four steps: a code-quality baseline, a reliable test safety-net, an objective feedback loop of code-health data and test outcomes, and letting agents build an evolving playbook of codebase-specific refactoring patterns.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: A reusable playbook for enterprises operationalizing AI code maintenance; implies demand for testing and metrics infrastructure.
insights.locator: InfoQ: How can we do refactoring at scale with agents?

insights.claim: Safeguards for AI-generated code must be fully automated and exposed to agents as local MCP servers or command-line tools, including linting, code coverage, mutation testing and higher-level metrics like Code Health.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Static analysis, testing and quality tooling get repositioned as agent infrastructure.
insights.locator: InfoQ: How do you safeguard AI-generated code?

insights.claim: Code quality at the module level is largely solved with current automation, and scaling AI-friendliness to the design and architectural level is the next big challenge.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: The next tooling frontier is architecture-level AI assistance; module-level quality tools risk commoditization.
insights.locator: By refactoring code, modularizing it and making it healthy
